title: Tool registry, toolsets, tool runtime, MCP
tldr: No single tool abstraction: 7 tool sources, 7 dispatch branches, and two dispatchers with different precedence orders (TLS-01, TLS-02).

Biggest kill: about 250 lines of plugin-authorization policy with stack-frame inspection inside tools/registry.py, duplicating PluginContext (TLS-07); plus the import-time compat surface in model_tools (TLS-08).

Biggest simplification: ToolEntry gets a typed context, a prepare() hook and behaviour metadata (pydantic-ai shape). Inline executors, the rewriter table, the skip_* flags and about 20 agent name-lists go away (TLS-01, 05, 10).
Seam answer: several abstractions, not one. A toolsets/RunContext shape deletes an estimated 2,000-2,500 lines.

findings.title: Seven tool sources with seven dispatch branches and two precedence orders; no single tool abstraction
findings.problem: Registry entries go through handle_function_call. 15 agent-state tools go through INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS, and most are also registered with registry handlers the agent path never calls (model_tools.py:941 stubs 4; delegate_tool.py:771 calls its handler a 'mirror'). Context-engine and memory-provider tools are not in the registry: two copy-pasted injectors append their schemas and each has its own dispatch branch. Connectors and the Tool Search bridge are special-cased inside handle_function_call. The sequential resolver orders sources inline > delegate > context-engine > memory > registry. The concurrent invoke_tool orders them todo/session_search/memory > memory provider > inline minus message_agent > registry, and has no context-engine branch; it is safe only because the parallel allowlist never admits those names. Every contributor adding an agent-aware tool, and every reviewer, pays to keep the two paths in agreement.
findings.move: Give handlers a typed ToolContext (agent handle, ids, messages, UI callbacks, enabled tool names). Register inline tools as ordinary ToolEntry handlers taking ctx. Memory providers and context engines expose a toolset object, combined with the registry view at agent build (CombinedToolset). Delete INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS, INVOKE_TOOL_PRE_MEMORY_MANAGER_NAMES, _AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS, the five-branch _resolve_sequential_dispatch, both schema injectors and the delegate mirror handler. One dispatcher remains.

reference.pattern: CombinedToolset over FunctionToolsets; every tool receives RunContext (_run_context.py:169)

findings.risk: Tool list bytes and order must stay identical per config (prompt cache). GUI callbacks must stay bound per agent. The memory 'gated off by toolset' rule (agent/memory_manager.py:115-135) must hold. Tests patching INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS and _resolve_sequential_dispatch must move.

findings.title: The tool-call pipeline runs at three layers, and four skip_* flags plus a ContextVar turn the inner layers off
findings.problem: Coercion, aliasing, request middleware, the pre_tool_call hook, ACP edit approval, execution middleware, post_tool_call and transform_tool_result are implemented in model_tools.handle_function_call, again in agent/tool_executor.py, and a third time in agent_runtime_helpers.invoke_tool. The outer layers suppress the inner ones with skip_pre_tool_call_hook, skip_tool_request_middleware, skip_tool_execution_middleware and the _post_tool_call_hook_suppressed ContextVar. A grep counts 13/7/6/2 mentions in model_tools/agent_runtime_helpers/tool_executor/connectors. PluginContext.dispatch_tool calls registry.dispatch directly and skips all of it. A new phase must be added in up to three places, and the 'hook fired twice or zero times' bug class follows.
findings.move: Create tools/tool_pipeline.py::call_tool(entry, args, ctx), which owns every phase once and in order. handle_function_call, the sequential executor, invoke_tool and PluginContext.dispatch_tool all call it. The executor keeps only display, timeout and parallelism. Delete the skip flags and the ContextVar.

reference.pattern: ToolManager.handle_call: one call path for every tool

findings.risk: Preserve the single-fire pre_tool_call contract and the phase order. Whether plugin dispatch_tool should run guards is an intent question (unverified).

findings.title: Toolset membership is declared twice (ToolEntry.toolset and static TOOLSETS lists), plus _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS, and the declarations disagree
findings.problem: get_toolset unions static lists with registry membership at runtime (toolsets.py:308-315). browser_cdp and browser_dialog register toolset 'browser-cdp' and browser_exec 'browser-use', while TOOLSETS['browser'] lists all three. _get_plugin_toolset_names then reports 'browser-cdp'/'browser-use' as plugin toolsets (toolsets.py:317-321). apply_layout and kanban_schedule are registered but appear in no static list. yb_* register under the bundle name 'hermes-yuanbao'. The contract tests that tools/AGENTS.md cites for this do not exist.
findings.move: Declare membership once, on ToolEntry.toolset. Add a core=True field and derive _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS from it. TOOLSETS keeps only composites (includes) and descriptions. Fix the three browser registrations. Add one invariant test: every static toolset resolves to at least one registered tool, and every built-in entry's toolset is a known key.

reference.pattern: registry_add stores identity and info once; lookups derive from it

findings.risk: Prompt-cache stability of the sorted tool list. hermes tools config keys must keep working. disabled_toolsets: [browser] must still strip browser_cdp.

findings.title: 20 hermes-<platform> bundles copy the core list; plugin platforms already get the same bundle synthesized
findings.problem: 17 of the 23 hermes-* entries are _bundle(description), meaning core plus nothing. hermes-gateway re-lists 19 bundle names by hand. hermes-yuanbao carries a dead 'module' key. Plugin platforms get the same bundle synthesized by _plugin_platform_bundle. hermes_cli/platforms.py repeats each default_toolset string. Adding a platform means editing three lists.
findings.move:
Synthesize hermes-

for built-in platforms through the plugin path: core plus tools whose toolset belongs to platform p. Delete the static entries, the hermes-gateway list and the per-platform default_toolset strings. Keep hermes-webhook, hermes-api-server and hermes-acp explicit.

reference.pattern: register_tools(register): registration in one place; bundles derive from it

findings.risk: Users' config.yaml names must still validate. Descriptions shown in the UI move to PLATFORMS.

findings.title: Schema assembly has 12 stages across 4 modules and two competing dynamic-schema mechanisms
findings.problem: Per-entry dynamic_schema_overrides covers 9 tools and the name-keyed _DYNAMIC_SCHEMA_REWRITERS covers 10. delegate_task and browser_exec use both. The discord rewriter calls getattr(module, string). Afterwards agent_init prunes, drops and appends four more times. Because the inputs are implicit, the memo key needs 10 fields, including an env var and a config.yaml stat. Answering 'what does the model see' means reading four modules. This is where prompt-cache breaks live (gist: I 333, C 44).
findings.move: Add one prepare(ctx, tool_def) -> tool_def | None hook on ToolEntry, with ctx carrying the available-name set and session facts. Add a toolset-level prepare for pruning. Delete dynamic_schema_overrides, _DYNAMIC_SCHEMA_REWRITERS and _compose_rewriters. The memo key becomes a hash of ctx, which makes the gist's Phase-5 prefix-stability check a pure-function test.

reference.pattern: PreparedToolset / ToolPrepareFunc (tools.py:106): prepare may drop or edit, not add or rename

findings.risk: Schemas must be byte-identical for an unchanged config. The 'never name an absent tool' rule must hold.

findings.title: mcp_tool and browser_tool siblings read facade globals through call-time proxies (630 reads; browser walks stack frames)
findings.problem: The split left all state in the facades. MCP siblings make 362 _core./_origin. reads (_core._lock x58, _core._servers x38). Browser siblings make 268 _bt./origin. reads, and that proxy calls sys._getframe on each access. mcp_tool.py holds 17 module dicts, 3 sets and 3 locks, and siblings write facade globals. The stated reason is test patching (106 + 125 patch sites). The mechanism is the same class as tui_gateway bind_module, and it hides the package from static analysis.
findings.move: Move the state into objects: tools/mcp_state.py::McpClientPool and tools/browser_sessions.py::BrowserSessions. Siblings import the instance and tests patch its attributes. Delete _OriginProxy, browser_tool_origin.py and the PEP 562 SDK loader.

reference.pattern: MCPToolset keeps connection state on the instance

findings.risk: About 231 test patch sites move. Profile-scoped MCP trust and the reconnect/refresh semantics must be preserved.

findings.title: The registry embeds plugin authorization with stack-frame inspection, duplicating PluginContext checks, and reaches into gateway/
findings.problem: About 250 lines of policy: _PluginOverridePolicy with CAS restore, module-to-scope maps, a __globals__/partial/__wrapped__ ownership walk, and sys._getframe(2) to identify deregister callers. PluginContext.register_tool already enforces the same opt-in and shadow rules. In-tree plugins never call registry.register directly. The registry also late-imports gateway.session_context, gateway.browser_control_broker, agent.secret_scope and model_tools, despite its 'no deps' docstring.
findings.move: Make the registry a scope-keyed store (register/deregister/restore by scope). Authorization lives only in PluginContext, which knows the plugin identity by construction. Callers pass the check_fn cache scope in.

reference.pattern: host hands the plugin a bound register callable; identity known without frame inspection

findings.risk: The no-override-without-opt-in rule and per-profile plugin isolation must hold for ctx callers. Third-party plugins importing tools.registry directly lose the guard (a policy call).

findings.title: Import-time backward-compat surface in model_tools and the registry state kept alive for it
findings.problem: TOOL_TO_TOOLSET_MAP and TOOLSET_REQUIREMENTS are import-time snapshots with 1 and 2 callers. Banner reads only check_fn presence. To serve it, the registry maintains _toolset_checks through register, deregister and restore, and the comment says it gates nothing. There are five one-line pass-throughs, legacy *_tools names, and a dead 'module' key.
findings.move: Delete _toolset_checks, get_toolset_requirements, both constants and the pass-throughs. Banner and doctor call registry.get_available_toolsets(). Drop the module key.
findings.risk: Banner's lazy-init versus disabled classification output must stay the same. batch_runner follows the seam 15 decision.

findings.title: _last_resolved_tool_names is a process-global channel for execute_code's allowed tools, saved and restored around delegation
findings.problem: Every get_tool_definitions call overwrites the global, including cache hits and other sessions' agents. execute_code falls back to it when no enabled_tools is passed. The agent paths always pass enabled_tools, so the global serves only code_kernel, code_execution_rpc and the hermes-tools MCP server. In a multi-session process the fallback can hand one session another session's tool set.
findings.move: Put enabled_tools in ToolContext. Non-agent callers pass an explicit catalog. Delete the global and the save/restore.

reference.pattern: per-run state travels in the context

findings.risk: Sandbox stubs must see the same names for agent calls. Check nested execute_code inside a delegated child.

findings.title: Tool behaviour metadata (parallel-safe, idempotent, mutating, failure-tolerant) lives in about 20 name lists in agent/
findings.problem: A census found 115 literals with two or more tool names in 44 non-test files. The lists drift. IDEMPOTENT_TOOL_NAMES hard-codes eight mcp_filesystem_* names from a third-party server. MUTATING and PROGRESS_RESET list send_message, which is deliberately unregistered, and legacy aliases (cronjob, todo, process). MCP already has per-tool read-only hints but is consulted through a side channel.
findings.move: Add typed ToolEntry fields: read_only, idempotent, sequential, failure_is_output. MCP fills them from annotations. Planners and guardrails read registry entries. Display tables stay.
findings.risk: Parallel batching must not widen. The path-overlap reader/writer rules stay code.

findings.title: process_registry.py mixes a 2,034-line service class, systemd plumbing and the process_manage tool, with an import-time home capture
findings.problem: One 2,898-line file holds the systemd scope probe and argv building, ProcessSession, the ProcessRegistry class (29 public methods), the module singleton imported by 45 non-test files, and the model tool schema and handler. CHECKPOINT_PATH captures get_hermes_home() at import, although _checkpoint_path() exists beside it.
findings.move: Split into tools/process_tool.py (schema and handler), tools/process_systemd.py and tools/process_registry.py (the service). Delete the import-time constant. Seam 09 owns the concurrency inside.

reference.pattern: services fetched from a container instead of module singletons

findings.risk: Test patch seams on tools.process_registry.* move. The _terminate_host_pid teardown order must be preserved.

findings.title: Tool discovery AST-parses source text (cached on disk per profile), and importing model_tools runs plugin discovery as a side effect
findings.problem: discover_builtin_tools ast-parses every tools/*.py looking for a literal registry.register at module level, with verdicts cached under HERMES_HOME keyed on mtime and size to save about 145 ms. A tool that registers via a helper is silently skipped. Any import of model_tools runs discovery plus discover_plugins(), which is why cli.py wraps it lazily. AGENTS.md calls the no-list design deliberate; this finding argues against that rule.
findings.move: Use an explicit tuple of built-in tool modules in tools/__init__.py, guarded by one invariant test against the tree. Plugin discovery becomes an explicit call at each entry point's startup, next to MCP discovery. Importing model_tools becomes side-effect free.

reference.pattern: explicit load_setuptools_entrypoints call; llm default plugins are an explicit list

findings.risk: Deterministic duplicate-name resolution must be kept. Every entry point must call discovery.

findings.title: tools/AGENTS.md makes false claims: no-deps registry, dispatch location, a stale toolset key list, contract tests that do not exist
findings.problem: The registry has late deps on gateway, agent and model_tools. handle_function_call lives in model_tools.py:876, not the registry. The key list names moa, rl and messaging (not keys) and omits about 25 real keys. The cited 'every registered tool has a toolset' and 'no schema description names a tool from another toolset' tests are absent. Agents trust this file.
findings.move: After TLS-03, the first claim becomes a real invariant test. Cut the key list and correct the dependency and dispatch sentences.

seam_answer: There are several tool abstractions, not one. ToolEntry has schema, handler, check_fn and toolset. But membership is declared again in TOOLSETS and _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS. 15 tools' real handlers live in INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS. Memory-provider and context-engine tools bypass the registry. The model-visible schema is rewritten by two mechanisms plus four agent-side passes. Behaviour facts live in name lists in agent/. The call pipeline exists three times. A pydantic-ai toolsets shape fixes this: a ToolEntry whose handler takes a typed RunContext, with a prepare() hook and sequential/read_only metadata, composed by a CombinedToolset filtered by session selection. It deletes INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS, _AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS, the five-branch resolver, the skip-flag protocol, _DYNAMIC_SCHEMA_REWRITERS, the static per-tool lists, about 20 behaviour sets and the process-global _last_resolved_tool_names: an estimated -2,000 to -2,500 lines. inspect_ai's registry supplies 'declare once, look up by name'. Plugin authorization belongs in PluginContext, not in the registry.

cross_seam.note: _run_async builds a fresh ThreadPoolExecutor and event loop per call under a running loop; MCP runs a separate long-lived loop thread. Two async bridges for one need.
process registry checkpoint path captured from get_hermes_home() at import
ctx.dispatch_tool calls registry.dispatch directly, skipping hooks, middleware, aliases and ACP edit approval
core toolsets.py hard-codes a spotify toolset whose tools come from plugins/spotify
agent.tools is post-processed in agent_init after get_tool_definitions; tool list ownership is split across two layers
tools import hermes_cli eagerly at module level; registry reaches into gateway
toolset_distributions.py and TOOL_TO_TOOLSET_MAP exist only for batch_runner
library code prints to stdout when quiet_mode=False
check_fn cache scope reads gateway session env (browser-control identity) inside the tool registry
